addressed_weaknesses: Novelty: stated explicitly that each rule builds on a standard idea and that the contribution is their combination into one procedure plus its systematic evaluation

Wide tolerance: added 'How to read a score when the tolerance is wide' — tolerance is 4.5-10.4 % of the lag range in every setting; delay reported separately; scores compared only with aTDS chance levels
300-s cap: stated that the cap is the user's choice of time resolution, not a property of the signals; aTDS sets lag range and tolerance for the chosen window

REM inversion: no ground truth; the mean-TDS change may reflect the wider tolerance, the significant-link contrast did not change; no longer counted as an improvement (Results, abstract, summary table)
Bartlett truncation and record-length dependence: added 'What the window does not capture'
Untested constants and missing generic baselines: Limitations now list the 0.3 rhythm threshold, the first-zero truncation, and the absence of GCC/coherence-based comparisons
Removed version-history references (v2.1, earlier rule); fixed the Bartlett 1946 reference
integrated_answers: Interpretation of scores with large tolerance: Methods (tolerance as fraction of lag range)
Why widen tolerance rather than lengthen window: Methods paragraph, linked to the oracle results
External evidence for the REM change: none; stated in Results
Cap from stage-episode lengths: suggested in Practical guidance as untested
Null keeping shared co-modulation, GCC/PHAT comparison, sensitivity of constants: not in the experimental log; stated as limitations, no new experiments added
